Subject: Throughput commitment & initial sizing questions — private GPU deployment

Hi Marco / Nimble infra team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, we put together a compact throughput commitment that maps your 99th-percentile SLA targets into a practical private GPU pool sizing and scaling strategy for your VPC deployment. The attached spreadsheet (throughput_commitment_matrix_v1.xlsx) has the baseline numbers; high-level summary below: 

- Target production workload: 1200 concurrent chat sessions (active prompt/response cycles) during peak windows
- Observed avg request size: ~600 tokens in / 350 tokens out (we used 1.7x token multiplier for planning)
- Latency SLO: 95% of responses < 400ms tail for single-turn generation (can accept fallback increment to 750ms during burst)
- Proposed steady-state capacity: 8x H100-equivalent workers (12GB q8 quantized profile) with continuous batching tuned for 4–8ms scheduling windows
- Burst strategy: +4 workers (warm pool) and autoscale policy driven by 5-min rolling ingress + KV cache hit thresholds

Networking notes: ensure MTU >= 9000 on your cross-host NICs for high-throughput KV/cache replication jobs; consider LACP bonding for redundant 100Gbps links. We flagged some perimeter items in network_mtu_checklist.pdf.

Can you confirm:
1) expected peak qps and average tokens-per-request for your chat flows during Black Friday–like scenarios?
2) whether your VPC has RDMA/InfiniBand available, or if we should plan for TCP-over-100Gbps only?

Next steps: once we have your traffic snapshot and NIC capabilities, our infra team (cc'd) will produce a final sizing calc and an SLA commit matrix for signature.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

> Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, we put together a compact throughput commitment...

Hi Vanessa,

Appreciate the concise plan. A few clarifications from our side after pulling last week's traffic:
- Peak concurrent sessions: 1,050 (spike to 1,600 for short bursts; see attached nimble_traffic_snapshot_20270219.csv)
- Tokens/request: median 520 in / 320 out, 95th pct ~ 1400 total tokens (we care about tail behavior)
- Network stack: we do not have RDMA in prod; two bonded 100Gbps NICs with Jumbo frames enabled (MTU 9000) between hosts in the same rack; cross-rack links are routed and occasionally hit 40Gbps.
- Storage/cache: we run a Redis cluster with 1ms avg local lookup; cross-host replication adds ~2–3ms on cross-rack hits.

Can Redwood provide a recommended warm-pool warmup strategy — how many KV cache priming calls are required per worker before it reaches expected tail latency? Also need to understand the SLA fallback behavior if we exceed the warm pool (hot scaling takes ~90–110s).

Thanks,

Vanessa / team,

Following Marco's data, I ran a quick sizing calc and attached the notes (sizing_calculation_notes_20270226.pdf). TL;DR:

- Baseline workers: 8 H100-equivalents covers steady-state for ~1,100 concurrent sessions with our batching (avg batch size 6, dynamic batching window 6ms) given their median token sizes.
- Tail coverage: to hit 95% < 400ms tail with cross-rack replication, add a warm pool of 6 hot workers and keep KV cache warm via a 60s rolling prime (see warmup sequence below). That yields < 420ms 99th for most traces; 95th comfortably < 350ms.
- Warmup sequence (recommended):
  1) boot worker, load model weights (30–45s for quantized profile),
  2) pre-warm KV cache: replay representative prompts from nimble_traffic_snapshot (approx 4k prefixes to achieve >85% hit), ~20–35s depending on cross-host latency,
  3) warm batch run: feed ~120 short inference jobs to stabilize CUDA kernels and cache, ~10–15s.
- Autoscale settings: scale-up on 5-min rolling CPU/GPU queue depth + sustained 90th qps > threshold; scale-down only after 10m of sustained low utilization. Protect against flapping with a 3-minute hold window.

Network considerations and constraints we called out:
- Cross-rack 40Gbps links are the main gating factor for sustained KV replication under heavy tail. For sustained >1.2k concurrent with large token sizes, advise either (a) reserve cross-rack capacity via routing policies, or (b) colocate a subset of workers in the same rack as primary cache replicas.
- MTU 9000 is good; confirm that all switches on the path honor jumbo frames (we saw intermittent drops in other customer infra where one switch was misconfigured).

Attachments: sizing_calculation_notes_20270226.pdf

Action items (owners):
- Marco (Nimble): confirm whether co-location of warm pool workers in primary rack is feasible (by 2027-02-28)
- Dev Patel (Redwood): produce a canary rollout plan with 5% traffic cutover and a rollback threshold for tail latency (due 2027-02-26)
- Vanessa: finalize SLA matrix and drive procurement redline (due 2027-03-02)

Hi Marco / team,

Excellent, thanks for the confirmation and the traffic snapshot. Quick recap and next steps:

- We will provision: 8 H100-equivalent steady workers + 6 warm pool workers (co-located recommendation pending Nimble confirmation).
- Canary: 5% of traffic for 30 minutes, monitor tail latency, p99 latency, token throughput, and cache hit ratio. Rollback if p99 > 750ms or cache hit ratio drops by >20%.
- Warmup: follow Laura's 3-step sequence; our canary automation will pre-warm the canary subset 10 minutes before traffic shift.
- Network: Marco to confirm rack co-location; Redwood to provide a short checklist for switch MTU checks (see network_mtu_checklist.pdf).

I'll kick off the SLA matrix and procurement doc once we get Marco's co-location answer. Proposed meeting to finalize: 2027-03-01 10:00 PT (30m) — does that work?
